dossier.purpose: Three independent code-indexing components read together. Revisions read: scip-code/scip tag v0.10.0 (1c2b6db); sourcegraph/zoekt main @ 153817f643cd (no tag in the shallow clone; _extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/.git/packed-refs:2); universal-ctags/ctags tag v6.2.1 @ b8eb0da41213 (_extra/universal-ctags__ctags/.git/packed-refs:2-3). (1) SCIP: a Protobuf schema (scip.proto) for language-agnostic source-code index data (symbols, occurrences with definition/reference roles, relationships such as implementation and type definition, diagnostics), bindings in 7 languages, and a Go `scip` CLI that lints, prints, snapshots, tests, summarizes and converts index files; it contains no indexers, no query service and no MCP or language-server code (README.md:3-15; cmd/scip/main.go:22-30). (2) Zoekt: a positional-trigram source-code search engine with indexers, a web UI, a JSON HTTP API and a gRPC API; it shells out to Universal Ctags for symbol ranges used in ranking and `sym:` queries (_extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/README.md:7-23,35-36,131-140). (3) Universal Ctags: a C tag-file generator (116 C files in parsers/ plus parsers/cxx/ and 28 optlib/*.ctags definitions) with u-ctags/e-ctags/etags/xref/JSON output, a `readtags` query tool and a JSON-lines `--_interactive` mode (_extra/universal-ctags__ctags/README.md:11-16,34-40; man/ctags.1.rst.in:309-319). None of the three trees contains an MCP server, a language-server (LSP) client/server, symbol-level edit tooling, or a Claude Code/Codex integration (greps for mcp, claude, codex, language server, LSP found only comments, language names and zoekt's contributor-facing AGENT.md). Only the three directories in the working tree were read; linked external pages (docs.sourcegraph.com, sourcegraph.com/security, ctags-nightly-build, etc.) were not opened.

claims.claim: SCIP is 'a language-agnostic protocol for indexing source code, which can be used to power code navigation functionality such as Go to definition, Find references, and Find implementations.'

Repository contents: a Protobuf schema (scip.proto); 'Rich Go and Rust bindings' with many utility functions for building tooling; auto-generated bindings for TypeScript and Haskell; and the `scip` CLI, 'which makes SCIP indexes a breeze to work with'.

Indexers that emit SCIP: scip-java (Java/Scala/Kotlin), scip-typescript, rust-analyzer, scip-clang, scip-ruby, scip-python, scip-dotnet, scip-dart, scip-php, debian-lsp. Other tools using SCIP: the Sourcegraph CLI (src-cli) and this repo's CLI.
CLI install: download binaries from the GitHub releases page, or `git clone https://github.com/scip-code/scip.git --depth=1; cd scip; go build ./cmd/scip`; usage via docs/CLI.md or --help.
Design doc (linked from the README): SCIP is 'a transmission format ... not a storage format for querying'.

Design doc non-goals: 'Support use cases involving code modifications' and 'Support efficient code navigation by itself' (navigation needs a bidirectional-lookup query engine); ease of writing consumers is also a non-goal.
Zoekt is a 'text search engine intended for use with source code' with fast substring and regexp matching and a query language with boolean operators (and, or, not), over one or many repositories.

Zoekt ranks results using code-related signals such as whether the match is on a symbol; 'Because of its general design based on trigram indexing and syntactic parsing, it works well for a variety of programming languages'.
Zoekt recommends installing Universal ctags because 'symbol information is a key signal in ranking search results'.
Zoekt web server serves a search UI at http://localhost:6070; with `-rpc` it exposes a JSON search API at /api/search; it also exposes a gRPC API supporting structured queries and streaming results.
Zoekt publishes a container image ghcr.io/sourcegraph/zoekt containing the Zoekt binaries, git and universal-ctags; default command is zoekt-webserver against /data/index.
Universal Ctags is 'a maintained implementation of ctags' that generates an index (tag file) of language objects in source files so that editors and other tools can locate them.
Major ctags features: more and improved language support (new C/C++ parser), fully extended optlib (define parsers from the command line), and interactive mode (experimental).
ctags builds with Autotools on GNU/Linux, OSX or Windows 10 WSL; a Homebrew formula is offered for Mac; nightly (Unix-like) and daily (Windows) builds come from separate repositories.

install.method: scip CLI release binary (Linux and macOS). One-liner from the draft-release notes template; assets are scip-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz. TAG is the release tag. On Linux arm64 `uname -m` typically prints aarch64, which this sed does not map to the published 'arm64' asset name.
install.command: env TAG="v0.10.0" OS="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" ARCH="$(uname -m | sed -e 's/x86_64/amd64/')" bash -c 'curl -L "https://github.com/scip-code/scip/releases/download/$TAG/scip-$OS-$ARCH.tar.gz"' | tar xzf - scip
git clone https://github.com/scip-code/scip.git --depth=1 && cd scip && go build ./cmd/scip

install.method: zoekt from source with Go (Linux; Go >= 1.25.9 with toolchain go1.26.5; also needs `git` on PATH and, for symbols, a universal-ctags binary reachable as `universal-ctags` or via CTAGS_COMMAND)
install.command: go install github.com/sourcegraph/zoekt/cmd/zoekt-git-index@latest && go install github.com/sourcegraph/zoekt/cmd/zoekt@latest && go install github.com/sourcegraph/zoekt/cmd/zoekt-webserver@latest

install.method: zoekt container image (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64; includes git and universal-ctags)

universal-ctags from source with Autotools (GNU/Linux, macOS, WSL). zoekt's doc/ctags.md additionally recommends `./configure --enable-json --enable-seccomp` (needs libjansson and libseccomp) for use with zoekt.
install.command: git clone https://github.com/universal-ctags/ctags.git && cd ctags && ./autogen.sh && ./configure && make && make install

code.architecture: SCIP (Go workspace go.work with 3 modules: root github.com/scip-code/scip, bindings/go/scip, reprolang): scip.proto is the wire format; buf.gen.yaml generates Go (bindings/go/scip/scip.pb.go), TypeScript (bindings/typescript/scip_pb.ts), Rust (bindings/rust/src/generated/), Haskell, C#, Java, Kotlin bindings and docs/scip.md. bindings/go/scip adds hand-written helpers: parse.go (streaming IndexVisitor), canonicalize.go, flatten.go, sort.go (FindOccurrences by line/character), sanitize.go, symbol*.go (parser/formatter), position.go/occurrence_range.go, source_file.go, testutil/ (snapshot formatter and the `scip test` runner). cmd/scip/*.go are thin urfave/cli commands over that library: lint.go (symbol table, relationship, range and duplicate checks), print.go (pretty/JSON dump), snapshot.go, stats.go (gocloc + percentiles), test.go, convert.go (experimental SQLite export: documents, chunks with zstd-compressed occurrence blobs, global_symbols, mentions, defn_enclosing_ranges). reprolang/ is a tree-sitter toy language plus indexer used only to generate test indexes (docs/Development.md:19-23). Real language indexers live in other repositories (README.md:35-46). SCIP data model: Index{metadata, documents[], external_symbols[]}; Document{relative_path, language, occurrences[], symbols[], optional text}; Occurrence{range, symbol, symbol_roles bitset, syntax_kind, diagnostics[], enclosing_range}; SymbolInformation{symbol, kind, display_name, documentation, relationships[], signature_documentation, enclosing_symbol}; Diagnostic is per-occurrence index-time data (scip.proto:740-741, 810-835). Zoekt (Go module github.com/sourcegraph/zoekt): root api.go (result types: FileMatch with repo, commit Version, branches, Line/ChunkMatches, Symbol{Sym,Kind,Parent,ParentKind}), query/ (parser and AST), index/ (shard builder; mmap'ed on-disk shards with positional trigram posting lists, IndexFormatVersion 16; ctags integration in index/ctags.go; scoring in index/score.go and contentprovider.go), search/ (directory searcher with an fsnotify shard watcher, search/watcher.go), gitindex/ (git tree -> shards, shells out to `git cat-file`), web/ (HTML UI, /healthz), internal/json (/api/search, /api/list), grpc/ (WebserverService), internal/ctags (wrapper over sourcegraph/go-ctags speaking ctags --_interactive; can also drive a separate `scip-ctags` binary via SCIP_CTAGS_COMMAND, whose source is in none of the three trees), cmd/* (19 binaries: indexers, indexservers, mirrors for GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Gerrit/Gitiles/Bitbucket Server, a Sourcegraph-specific indexserver). Universal Ctags (C, Autotools): main/ core (options, parse, entry, lregex regex engine, writer-{ctags,etags,json,xref}.c, interactive loop, seccomp), parsers/ (116 .c files, plus parsers/cxx/ with 23 .c files), optlib/ (28 regex/optscript-defined parsers), libreadtags/, extra-cmds/ (readtags), dsl/ (optscript), vendored gnulib/.

claim_checks.claim: The `scip` CLI 'makes SCIP indexes a breeze to work with' (README.md:14-15); `expt-convert` converts an index to SQLite for inspection (docs/CLI.md:158-179).
claim_checks.evidence: Commands exist and match docs/CLI.md:28-35. `print --json` dumps the whole index (cmd/scip/print.go:64-66). Every command loads the entire index into memory via io.ReadAll + proto.Unmarshal (cmd/scip/option_from.go:31-37) even though a streaming parser exists (bindings/go/scip/parse.go:26-29). expt-convert is marked EXPERIMENTAL; it creates `signature` and `relationships` columns but never writes them, skips external and local symbols, and stores occurrences as zstd-compressed protobuf blobs in chunks of about 200 (cmd/scip/convert.go:26, 198-200, 289-291, 315, 423-486), so implementation/type-definition relationships are not queryable from the SQLite output at v0.10.0.

claim_checks.claim: Several indexers currently emit SCIP data: scip-java, scip-typescript, rust-analyzer, scip-clang, scip-ruby, scip-python, scip-dotnet, scip-dart, scip-php, debian-lsp (README.md:35-46).
claim_checks.evidence: Indexers live in other repositories, not in the working tree. Indirect evidence only: .github/workflows/scip-examples.yaml:23-50 runs scip-java, scip-python, scip-typescript, scip-ruby, scip-clang and scip-dotnet nightly against 7 OSS repos (a Kotlin target is commented out with 'scip-java has problems with indexing Kotlin codebase', lines 27-30); scip-dart, scip-php, rust-analyzer and debian-lsp are not exercised here.

claim_checks.claim: scip CLI is available as release binaries or via `go build ./cmd/scip` (README.md:56-63).
claim_checks.evidence: release.yaml:246-304 builds linux/darwin x amd64/arm64 tarballs with a .sha256 each; go.mod:3 requires Go 1.25.0; a local build prints a '-dev' version with VCS info unless -X main.Reproducible=true is set (cmd/scip/main.go:35-58; release.yaml:285). No Windows asset. The curl one-liner in the release notes template maps only x86_64 to amd64 (release.yaml:80), so a Linux arm64 host reporting aarch64 would not match the published scip-linux-arm64 name.

claim_checks.claim: Zoekt's query language has boolean operators 'and, or, not' (_extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/README.md:15-17).
claim_checks.evidence: The parser reserves only `or` (query/parse.go:533-535); negation is the `-` prefix; conjunction is implicit; doc/query_syntax.md:91-92 states 'The word `and` is not an operator; it is interpreted as a search term.'

claim_checks.claim: Zoekt exposes a JSON API with -rpc, a gRPC API, and a container image that runs zoekt-webserver (_extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/README.md:112-140).
claim_checks.evidence: -rpc defaults to false (cmd/zoekt-webserver/main.go:135) and mounts /api/ (web/server.go:242-244) serving /search and /list (internal/json/json.go:20-21); gRPC WebserverService has Search, StreamSearch, List (grpc/protos/zoekt/webserver/v1/webserver.proto:11-18) and is always multiplexed on the same port (main.go:289-291). Caveat not in the README: the image's default CMD is `zoekt-webserver -index /data/index -pprof -rpc` (Dockerfile:51), so the JSON API and pprof are enabled by default in the container; doc/design.md:309-315 describes the UI as unauthenticated and no auth code appears in web/.

claim_checks.claim: Zoekt uses ctags symbol info as a ranking signal and 'universal ctags will be called using seccomp' (README.md:35-36; doc/ctags.md:14-16).
claim_checks.evidence: Ranking use is confirmed: scoreSymbol = 7000 and symbol-kind boosts (index/contentprovider.go:596, 717-720; index/score.go:152-164). zoekt starts ctags through github.com/sourcegraph/go-ctags with only Options{Bin} set (internal/ctags/parser.go:99-105) and requires the binary to report +interactive (internal/ctags/parser_bins.go:104-105); whether sandbox mode is requested happens inside that dependency, which is not in the tree, so the seccomp claim is not checkable here. ctags itself implements the sandbox (_extra/universal-ctags__ctags/main/seccomp.c:20-75).

claim_checks.claim: ctags generates reference tags only in limited areas, and interactive mode (JSON over stdio) is experimental (_extra/universal-ctags__ctags/README.md:40; man/ctags.1.rst.in:1655-1661).
claim_checks.evidence: Man page: reference-tag generation 'is new and limited to specific areas of specific languages' (man/ctags.1.rst.in:1655-1661); XTAG_REFERENCE_TAGS appears in 8 parsers/*.c files (python, cpreprocessor, c-based, gdscript, m4, ldscript, dtd, systemdunit). The interactive loop reads JSON-lines requests and is compiled only with libjansson (main/main.c:393-460; docs/interactive-mode.rst:7-13); configure auto-detects jansson and libseccomp instead of requiring them (configure.ac:818-838), so a default build can lack JSON output, interactive mode and the sandbox, and zoekt rejects a ctags without +interactive.

risks: Scope: none of the three trees contains an MCP server, language-server (LSP) client/server code, symbol-level edit tooling, or a Claude Code/Codex integration (greps for mcp|claude|codex|language server|LSP found only comments, language names and zoekt's contributor-facing AGENT.md:1-26 / .agents/setup). SCIP lists code modification and 'efficient code navigation by itself' as non-goals (docs/DESIGN.md:49-54, 63-71) and its diagnostics are index-time Occurrence.diagnostics (scip.proto:740-741, 810-835), not live post-edit diagnostics; any definition/reference/diagnostic answer from this bundle depends on separately built indexes.

Precision and freshness limits of structural indexes: ctags documents reference tags as 'new and limited to specific areas of specific languages' (_extra/universal-ctags__ctags/man/ctags.1.rst.in:1655-1661); zoekt's ctags-derived symbol offsets are best-effort ('For short symbol names, we will often determine the wrong offset'; Go multi-line declarations are skipped; _extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/index/ctags.go:152-158) and its results are text matches over whatever was last indexed from git branches (zoekt-git-index default -branches HEAD, cmd/zoekt-git-index/main.go:40; index refresh needs a re-run or zoekt-indexserver); SCIP precision depends on third-party indexers outside this repo (README.md:35-46; a Kotlin target is disabled in CI, scip-examples.yaml:27-30) and Metadata carries no commit/revision field to detect a stale index (scip.proto:41-54).

SCIP CLI/consumer gaps and write behaviour: no definition/reference lookup command (cmd/scip/main.go:22-30); the CLI loads the whole index into memory (cmd/scip/option_from.go:31-37) although a streaming parser exists (bindings/go/scip/parse.go:26-29); `expt-convert` is EXPERIMENTAL, never populates its signature/relationships columns, skips external and local symbols and stores occurrences as zstd blobs (cmd/scip/convert.go:198-200, 289-291, 315, 469-486); `scip snapshot` runs os.RemoveAll on its --to directory (default scip-snapshot) before writing (cmd/scip/snapshot.go:68) and `expt-convert` truncates its output file (convert.go:87).

zoekt network exposure and defaults: zoekt-webserver listens on ':6070' (all interfaces) by default (cmd/zoekt-webserver/main.go:132), serves indexed source via HTML, optional JSON API and always-on multiplexed gRPC (main.go:134-138, 289-291), and doc/design.md:309-315 describes the UI as unauthenticated (no auth code found in web/); the container image's default CMD enables -rpc and -pprof (Dockerfile:51); debugserver sets trace.AuthRequest to always allow (internal/debugserver/debug.go:58-60) and serves /metrics, /vars, /gc and /freeosmemory without auth (:55-85).

zoekt runtime dependencies and release hygiene: symbols require a universal-ctags binary built with +interactive on PATH as `universal-ctags` or via CTAGS_COMMAND (index/builder.go:290-300; internal/ctags/parser_bins.go:104-105); if none is found indexing proceeds without symbols unless -require_ctags is set, and ctags errors are otherwise logged and ignored (index/builder.go:969-978; index/ctags.go:73-81); `git` must be on PATH (gitindex/catfile.go:41); the image pins a ctags nightly dated 2024.01.07 (install-ctags-alpine.sh:10-15); distribution is `go install @latest` plus a container built from main/v* with no signing or attestation steps (docker.yml); Dockerfile:25 stamps a Version symbol that does not match index.Version (index/shard_builder.go:45-46); go.mod needs Go 1.25.9/toolchain 1.26.5 and has 138 requirements (go.mod:150-152); zoekt is read at main HEAD 153817f with no tag visible.

universal-ctags is C code parsing untrusted source: 6.2.1 is a bugfix release for crashes (R6 parser NULL dereference, Ada crash at EOF, C++ recursion limit; NEWS.rst:5-6, 21-39, 45-57); the seccomp sandbox exists only for `--_interactive=sandbox` on Linux, needs libseccomp and libjansson at build time, accepts only inline (stdin) content requests, and macOS support is a TODO (docs/interactive-mode.rst:71-104; main/seccomp.c:20-79; main/main.c:456-459); default `./configure` auto-detects rather than requires these (configure.ac:818-838); README calls interactive mode experimental (README.md:40); ctags auto-loads ./.ctags.d/*.ctags from the current directory (README.md:110-111); no security policy file.

Release integrity and maintenance: SCIP CLI tarballs ship only .sha256 files, no signatures/attestations (release.yaml:290-304), workflow actions are tag-pinned not SHA-pinned (0 SHA-pinned uses in .github/), schema is pre-1.0 (v0.10.0; ProtocolVersion has only an Unspecified value, scip.proto:56-58) and buf.yaml breaking-change rules are not run in CI; protocol changes need review by three CODEOWNERS handles (.github/CODEOWNERS:1-2); README/Development docs have drifted from the tree (README.md:13 omits JVM/.NET bindings; docs/Development.md:18 cites a nonexistent cmd/scip/tests/). ctags releases are manual tags and tarballs (docs/releasing.rst:75-95) with weekly auto-tags (tagging.yml:3-15) and no documented checksums/signatures; zoekt and ctags binaries come from workflows/repos that are not signed or not in the tree.

Licensing mix: scip and zoekt are Apache-2.0 (LICENSE; _extra/sourcegraph__zoekt/LICENSE); universal-ctags is GPL-2.0-or-later (COPYING; main/options.c:536-541) with some bundled files under other terms (dsl/es.c MIT-style permission notice, dsl/es.c:1-12; main/sort_r.h and main/portable-scandir.c public domain). zoekt's container image bundles a ctags binary alongside the Apache-2.0 zoekt binaries (Dockerfile:33-36; install-ctags-alpine.sh:3-50), while zoekt otherwise runs ctags as a separate process over stdio (internal/ctags/parser.go:99-105).

checks.statement: scip CLI release binary (Linux and macOS): `env TAG="v0.10.0" OS="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" ARCH="$(uname -m | sed -e 's/x86_64/amd64/')" bash -c 'curl -L "https://github.com/scip-code/scip/releases/download/$TAG/scip-$OS-$ARCH.tar.gz"' | tar xzf - scip`; assets are scip-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz; on Linux arm64 `uname -m` prints aarch64, which the sed does not map to the published 'arm64' name.
checks.note: release.yaml:76-81 echo lines unescape to exactly this command, with TAG filled from cmd/scip/version.txt (0.10.0; HEAD 1c2b6db = refs/tags/v0.10.0 in .git/packed-refs:2). Build matrix release.yaml:253-268 produces scip-linux-amd64, scip-linux-arm64, scip-darwin-arm64, scip-darwin-amd64, packed as $ASSET.tar.gz containing `scip` and LICENSE (:290), so `tar xzf - scip` extracts the binary. The sed at :79 maps only x86_64, so the aarch64 caveat is correct. README.md:56 links the releases page. The from-source alternative also holds: README.md:59-63 matches, and go.mod:3 and go.work:1 both say go 1.25.0. Nit: the asset names are at release.yaml:253-268/290, not inside 73-82.

LICENSE:1-2 is the Apache License, Version 2.0, and every scip package manifest agrees (bindings/rust/Cargo.toml:5, bindings/typescript/package.json:11, bindings/haskell/scip.cabal:13, bindings/dotnet/Scip.csproj:28, bindings/java/pom.xml:18-23, bindings/kotlin/pom.xml:20-25, flake.nix:39 asl20). zoekt LICENSE:1-2 is Apache 2.0. ctags COPYING:1-2 is GNU GPL Version 2; main/cmd.c:4-5 says 'GNU General Public License version 2 or (at your option) any later version', and main/options.c:536-541 says 'either version 2 ... of the License, or (at your option) any later version', which is GPL-2.0-or-later.

checks.statement: SCIP can power Go to definition, Find references and Find implementations (README.md:3-6) - verified: partial. The schema carries symbol roles and is_reference/is_implementation/is_type_definition/is_definition relationships, but the repo ships no navigation/query component (CLI: lint, print, snapshot, stats, test, expt-convert), efficient navigation by itself and code modification are non-goals, the Go bindings offer helpers such as FindOccurrences, indexers live in other repos, text is not stored by default, Metadata has no revision field, and diagnostics are index-time Occurrence.diagnostics.
checks.note: Every cited line checks out. README.md:3-6 has the quoted sentence. scip.proto:524-546 SymbolRole lists Definition, Import, WriteAccess, ReadAccess, Generated, Test, ForwardDefinition. :465-517 Relationship has the four booleans, with comments tying them to Find references/implementations and Go to (type) definition. symbol_roles is :728 inside Occurrence (:692-806), and :740-741 is per-occurrence diagnostics. :101-106 says indexers are not expected to include text by default. Metadata at :41-54 has only version/tool_info/project_root/text_document_encoding. main.go:22-30 registers lint, print, snapshot, stats, test and convert, and convert.go:33 names it expt-convert. DESIGN.md:49-54 and :63-71 are the code-modification and 'efficient code navigation by itself' non-goals. sort.go:48 is FindOccurrences; the non-generated Go bindings have no cross-document definition/reference lookup (only FindSymbol, FindSymbolBinarySearch, Document.SymbolTable, canonicalize/flatten/sort helpers). README.md:35-46 links every indexer to an external repo. 'partial' is a fair label.
